I think most of his points can be satisfactorily explained, honestly.

TFA was exactly the film it needed to be because of how horrible the prequels were. Don't ever forget that the world needed an apology for that drek, an assurance that the new movies would understand what everyone loved about the original films.

I mean this sincerely: blame Lucas for what TFA had to be. He severely damaged the IP for anyone but undiscerning children with those horrible CGI pieces of shit. If the prequels had been anywhere near the quality of the original trilogy, TFA wouldn't have needed so many "hey, remember this thing you loved about the good movies?!" moments. (And yes, it had too many.)

I'm going through his points one at a time.

The new characters are laughably shallow and never even get to know each other by the film's climax.

The characters in A New Hope weren't much better developed. They were character types, which made us feel like we knew them, but they didn't get a ton of development.

And that's okay. Star Wars is a "modern" take on adventure serials. The characterization in those wasn't great, either. There's a reason you couldn't take Indiana Jones's hat away from him in a new film: he is the hat, jacket, and whip. Otherwise he's a stock character.

The original films also had great actors in stock roles. That helps immensely to create likable characters. TFA? I think they were pretty good. Not as good as the originals, but better than the cast of the prequels. (But that was mostly the script.)

The 'plot' is a bit too fucking familiar.

Already answered in my other post.

The universe feels EXACTLY the same as it did in the original trilogy, pretty much making Luke, Han, and Leia's struggle in the original films pointless. Everything even LOOKS the same.

No it doesn't. The First Order, for example, has much more modern-looking armor. BB-8's design is totally unique for the series. Even the X-Wings look slightly different.

People have complained the "visual footprint" of the series doesn't look right, then say shit like this. You can't have it both ways.

Just unforgivably lazy. I expect MUCH more from a Star Wars film. TFA outright lacks any artistic vision and sums up everything that is wrong with the modern film industry.

All opinion.

As opposed to the totally believable victory of rock-wielding space teddy bears over the Empire in RotJ.

How the fuck could Rey fly and maintain the Millennium Falcon with such expertise, despite having NO apparent experience? The writers don't even bother to write in ONE line of dialogue that could possibly explain this.

This is a good point, but it's one that may be explained in a later film. We don't know much about Rey's backstory yet.

We do know she knows technology and ships from her salvage work. Flying them? Not sure.

A weapon that harnesses the power of the fucking sun? That's a plot device ripped out of Transfomers 2. Think about that. a plot device from TRANSFORMERS 2. In a STAR WARS film.

A super big Death Star. It this a parody?

This is just whining that he didn't like a plot element and doesn't deserve a response.

Oh, and Rey using Jedi mind tricks, let alone KNOWING about them without any apparent training? Good joke.

Everyone knows about the Jedi and their exploits. But they're thought to be myths at this point.

Rey had some sort of Force-related flash of knowledge or whatever at the Not Cantina. Might that explain some of this? Especially if we find out her parentage connects her strongly to the Force?

And how about that overly emotional acting/direction? Finn passionately yelling out "REYYYYY!!!!" despite knowing next to NOTHING about her? How the fuck do people overlook this? How could anyone buy that?

How about they spent a ton of time together?

Ever see Broken Arrow? Not a GREAT film, but not a bad one for a John Woo flick. The hero and the female lead don't know each other's names (or anything else) before the end. But they spent time together, so they kinda know one another. This is how human relationships work.

Han Solo and Chewbacca happen to come across the Millennium Falcon in the middle of space? Space is kind of a big place. That's kind of a bit unbelievable if you ask me. Well, maybe the Force led them to each other, right?

This is a good point unless they were looking for the Falcon in that area of space for a reason. We don't know if that's the case yet. (It may even be in the canon novelization, which admittedly would mean they failed to integrate it into the film adequately.)

Finn doesn't come across as a Stormtrooper who was indoctrinated since childhood. Like, at all. Wouldn't you expect him to share more personality traits with the Terminator than with Jar Jar Binks?

I completely agree with this point. It was one of my biggest complaints about the film.

But... if these guys were living on a base together like any military base, wouldn't they pal around? Might that explain why he isn't robotic like Opiate? We don't know that Finn was taken out of a fucking lab right before the film begins. Sure, he shouldn't have been so street smart as he was in the film given his origins, but...

Poe Dameron: Being a good pilot and looking suave doesn't make your character good.

Indiana Jones: being good with a whip and looking suave doesn't make your character good.

And finally, Kylo Ren is a little bitch. This became clear during that first interrogation scene with Poe at the burning village. The "So who talks first?" scene erases any menace from his character just five minutes into the fucking film. And his Force mind-fuck scenes were outright awkward to watch.

Dumbass. Kylo is NOT Vader. That's the point. He wants to be, but he isn't. And that makes his character interesting instead of just a clone of the baddies we've already seen. Are you complaining now that something WASN'T the same between ANH and TFA?

Fuck this abysmal film. An absolute disgrace to the Star Wars legacy. No fan-made solutions to the film's long list of plot holes will change how underwhelming it is.
